title: Stellar mass loss cannot hide ASASSN-14ko orbital decay through the debris return time unless the star is nearly destroyed, but it fits the levelled eRASSt J0456-20 recurrence with a constant orbit
abstract: Question: the ASASSN-14ko flare period decreased before 2020 and then stalled (constant 108.44-d X-ray dip clock). A pre-dip delay change can hide orbital decay in principle. Can the star, which loses mass at each passage, supply it? Approach: the most bound debris returns P(1+x)^-1.5 after pericentre, x being the frozen-in energy spread over the orbital binding energy, so the delay changes only through x, at most 0.279 P (30 d) per unit ln x. We fitted a clock in which x follows the stellar mass (mass-radius exponent zeta) and the mass falls in proportion to the measured flare fluences, with stellar survival, to signed campaign timing sets of ASASSN-14ko (40 points, 2014-2026) and eRASSt J0456-20 (7 cycles). Results: hidden decay in 2020-2024 needs a change of ln x of at least 0.15-0.39 (14-32 percent mass loss for a convective star). With a constant orbit the fluence clock fits ASASSN-14ko worse than a constant Pdot (-2 ln L 254 vs 214; two-break clock 184). Continued decay at the published rate comes within Delta(-2 ln L) = 4 of a free clock only if the star loses 99.9 percent of its mass by 2026 and shrinks on mass loss, which would stop the stripping; for a convective star the gap is at least 5.4. In 20 fluence-imputation draws every such solution needs at least 98 percent mass loss (80 percent for the weakest decrease rate). For eRASSt J0456-20, a constant 191.5-d orbit and a convective star fit (chi2 1.2) if about 90 percent of the star left at the first observed passage and the star was nearly gone by cycle 7, in agreement with its fading flares and 2024 non-detection. Thus the J0456-20 levelling can be a debris-return effect of a dying star, while the ASASSN-14ko stall is a stall of the orbit or of a non-stellar delay. Limitations: frozen-in spread, one power-law stellar response, stripped mass proportional to fluence, imputed fluences, unknown J0456-20 cycle-1 fluence, no tidal-heating model, no data for the 2026 flares.
